newsitem.title: USA: Merck halts two highest-dosage Zocor trials.
newsitem.headline: Merck halts two highest-dosage Zocor trials.

text.p: Merck & Co Inc said Monday it had halted two highest-dose studies of a new 160 mg formulation of its cholesterol-lowering medication Zocor because of side effects.
However, the company, which already markets a 40 mg version said it intended to seek seek FDA approval for a medium-dosage tablet by August 1.
Merck said Phase III trials of 80 mg tablets with 1,000 patients worldwide showed a good safety profile and the expected increase in efficacy over the 40 mg version now on the market.

But Merck said it was discontinuing studies with a 160 mg dose of Zocor involving about 400 patients because three patients during the past two weeks had developed rhabdomyolysis, a rare skeletal muscle fiber injury causing pain and weakness.

"The incidence of this side effect appeared to have been about one percent," the company said, which it described as a "relatively low incidence." But the trials were halted, it added, because patients had required hospitalization.
Merck, noting that an earlier study of the 160 mg formulation showed no cases of rhabdomyolysis in 130 patients, said it would decide later whether to resume trials at the 160 mg dose.

The maximum currently available 40 mg dose of Zocor produces an average 40 percent reduction in LDL cholesterol, Merck said, adding trials with the 80 mg tablet showed an average reduction of 47 percent.
